message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties**

| Property | Value | Notes |
|----------|-------|-------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 | Only one proton in the nucleus. |
| **Isotopes** | H‑1 (protium), H‑2 (deuterium), H‑3 (tritium) | Deuterium and tritium have one neutron each; tritium is radioactive. |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.00794 u (average) | Weighted average of isotopic masses. |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ | One valence electron. |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | Highest among all elements. |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) | Energy to remove the single valence electron. |
| **Second ionization energy** | 27.211 eV | Requires breaking the 1s² core. |
| **Electron affinity** | 72.8 kJ mol⁻¹ | Energy released when an electron is added. |
| **Atomic radius** | ~37 pm | Smallest atomic radius. |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) | Extremely low; boils at ~20 K. |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) | Solidifies at ~14 K. |
| **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ | Lightest gas; less than 1/10 the density of air. |
| **Molar volume at STP** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ | Standard molar volume for gases. |
| **State at room temperature** | Gas | Colorless, odorless, tasteless. |
| **Flammability** | Extremely flammable | Forms explosive mixtures with air (1–4 % H₂ in air). |
| **Reactivity** | Forms hydrides (e.g., NaH, CaH₂) and acids (e.g., HCl, H₂SO₄). | Strong reducing agent in many reactions. |
| **Bonding** | Diatomic (H₂) under normal conditions | Covalent bond with a bond dissociation energy of 436 kJ mol⁻¹. |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman, Balmer series | Prominent in stellar spectra; key in astrophysics. |
| **Role in stars** | Fusion fuel | Proton–proton chain and CNO cycle convert H into He. |
| **Applications** | Fuel cell technology, rocket propellant, hydrogenation reactions, medical imaging (tritium). | Widely used in industry and research. |

### Quick Summary

- **Lightest element**: only one proton and one electron (except for isotopes).
- **Highly reactive**: forms compounds with almost all other elements; reacts vigorously with oxygen, halogens, and many metals.
- **Physical extremes**: boils and melts at very low temperatures; extremely low density.
- **Chemical versatility**: participates in redox reactions, forms hydrides, acids, and organohydrogen compounds.
- **Astrophysical importance**: main fuel for stellar fusion; spectral lines are diagnostic of stellar composition.

These properties make hydrogen unique among the elements, enabling its use in diverse fields from energy production to materials science.
